text:
zoe_cs: Heads-up: onboarding account 'nebula' seeing bursts of 429s and a few 401s during their serverless rollout. Happening only in ap-southeast-1 and triggered when they flip a feature flag.

chad_eng: Can you paste the gateway log sample? 429+401 together usually means token churn + preflight fanout. Any CDN/proxy in front of their backend?

zoe_cs: Snippet: `2026-03-18T09:12:01Z GET /v1/preflight 429 {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","scope":"preflight"}` and a later `401 {"error":"invalid_token"}`. They use our Node serverless adapter and mint ephemeral tokens per-request (ttl=15s).

lara_oncall: TTL=15s is very short for cold-started serverless fleets. If many lambdas boot and each requests a token + calls preflight, you'll spike the preflight bucket. Any warmup or token caching?

chad_eng: Looks like their middleware fetches a token per invocation (synchronous) and the adapter calls SDK.init which triggers preflight. Two fixes: 1) cache tokens in the function/memory with a small grace period 2) preload a shared token using a short-lived in-memory cache for the life of the container. Also increase TTL >=60s.

zoe_cs: I gave them a small patch to memoize token and defer preflight until after first user interaction. Example diff: `const token = cached.get() || await backend.fetchToken(); cached.set(token, ttl-5000);`

lara_oncall: Also recommend SDK flag PREFLIGHT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 and PREFLIGHT_BACKOFF_MS=200. If they can't change backend, add client-side jitter and exponential backoff on preflight.

chad_eng: We reproduced with 250 cold containers and saw the same 429 spike. With token cache + PREFLIGHT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 the spike disappeared in our test.

ci-bot: ci: deployed patch branch serverless-token-cache -> staging (job 5123).

zoe_cs: Customer applied the token cache and bumping TTL to 90s. After a 30-minute rollout to 1200 users the 429s stopped. They're happy and will schedule a broader enablement run. :white_check_mark:

chad_eng: I'll add a short KB: "Serverless onboarding: avoid per-invocation ephemeral tokens; cache in-container; increase TTL; cap preflight concurrency." Also flag product to add safer defaults for serverless adapters.

lara_oncall: Marking account health: at-risk -> stabilizing. Follow-up: recommend console telemetry for token-fetch rates per app.
